item.title: WWII explosives detonate in France amid wildfires: "Sound of war"
item.description: The munitions, both German and French, consist mainly of mortar shells, along with some high-explosive anti-tank shells.

item.title: Trump threatens Iran with "decapitation" as Houthis claim strike on Saudi airport
item.description: Trump threatened Tehran with "decapitation" Monday, before Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis claimed to have struck a Saudi airport.

item.title: Trump raises concerns in call with Rep. Max Miller amid abuse allegations
item.description: Ohio Rep. Max Miller's reelection campaign has been upended by allegations Miller assaulted his ex-wife, Emily Moreno, and their 2-year-old daughter.

item.title: New details on Twin Falls In-N-Out shooting after 3 killed, 7 wounded
item.description: The suspect, identified as 24-year-old Chad Williams, died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound, police said.

item.title: Senate candidate Haley Stevens stands firm on backing U.S. military aid to Israel
item.description: Michigan Rep. Haley Stevens, one of two Democrats in the primary for her party's Senate nomination, stands firm on backing U.S. military aid to Israel and claims opponent Abdul El-Sayed doesn't recognize Israel's right to exist.

item.title: Why So Many Young People No Longer Believe Hard Work Pays Off | Money Moves with Jill Schlesinger
item.description: A growing number of young Americans no longer believe that ambition and hard work lead to success. Jill Schlesinger, Mark Talercio, and special guest host Kayla Sabbagh of Greenspring Advisors explain why that mindset can become a self-fulfilling prophecy and why believing you have agency over your future is essential to both your financial success and your mental health. Plus: they respond to a fiery YouTube comment about inheritance, family expectations, and leaving your money to charity.

item.title: 3 lions die at zoo as Japan bakes in "cruelly hot" summer
item.description: Ten of the 16 lions in Tama Zoological Park have suffered symptoms such as "loss of appetite and decreased activity" since mid-July, and three lionesses died, the zoo said.

item.title: Ukrainian drone strike on Russian warehouses in Moscow region kills 5
item.description: Ukraine has conducted long-range strikes targeting civilian infrastructure in Russia, and in recent weeks stepped up attacks on warehouses belonging to the Russian e-commerce giant Wildberries.

item.title: What to know about primaries in 5 states today: Michigan, Virginia and more
item.description: Voters are going to the polls Tuesday in five states: Michigan, Virginia, Missouri, Kansas and Washington.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy's diary excerpts read at trial: "I feel like I'm drowning"
item.description: The Lindsay Clancy trial​ resumed with excerpts from her diary and testimony from doctors who treated Clancy and her children on the night of the murders.

item.title: Arson arrest in one of the devastating Spokane area wildfires
item.description: More than 700 buildings in the Spokane area have been destroyed and 400 more haven't been assessed, officials said as three fires burned in the area and an arrest was made in connection with one of them.

item.title: Sen. Moreno says ex-son-in-law Max Miller shouldn't serve in Congress
item.description: GOP Sen. Bernie Moreno of Ohio said his former son-in-law, Rep. Max Miller, shouldn't serve in Congress amid swirling abuse claims, as Miller vowed to stay in the race for another term and strongly denied all allegations of misconduct.

item.title: Trump says Jeanine Pirro "choked" in dropping Reflecting Pool cases
item.description: "She folded like an umbrella," President Trump said of Jeanine Pirro, U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia.

item.title: "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" continues Hollywood's hot streak at the box office
item.description: "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" leapt straight to the top of the box office this weekend. Its $360 million opening weekend debut is the biggest in U.S. history. Marlow Stern, chief correspondent at Variety, joins CBS News to discuss all the latest movie news.

item.title: Most federal workers say they wouldn't enter public service again, survey finds
item.description: According to the National Active and Retired Federal Employees Association, 64% of workers say it's unlikely they would choose a federal career again. CBS News MoneyWatch reporter Megan Cerullo has more.

item.title: Latest on In-N-Out Idaho shooting that killed 3 as police search for motive
item.description: Three people were killed by a 24-year-old gunman at an In-N-Out in Twin Falls, Idaho, on Saturday. Lilia Luciano breaks down what we know.

item.title: More Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool charges dropped by Pirro's office
item.description: Since Friday, D.C. U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro's office has dropped charges against three more people accused of vandalism.

item.title: Senate candidate El-Sayed questions assumption Michigan voters are moderates
item.description: Populist Abdul El-Sayed and Rep. Haley Stevens top the Democratic field going into Tuesday's Senate primary. Former Rep. Mike Rogers is running unopposed for the GOP nomination.

item.title: El-Sayed and Stevens make final pitches before Democratic Michigan Senate primary
item.description: Dr. Abdul El-Sayed and Rep. Haley Stevens are in the final throws of their Democratic Senate primary in Michigan. CBS News' Aaron Navarro reports.

item.title: Michigan reports 2 cyclosporiasis deaths as cases top 18,000 nationwide
item.description: Two people have died of cyclosporiasis in Michigan, officials said Monday, as the state battles the worst outbreak of the disease in the country. Carter Evans has the details.

item.title: Justice Dept. moves to dismiss Jan. 6 class action lawsuit
item.description: The Justice Department argued that the Jan. 6, 2021, rioters had until Jan. 6, 2023, to sue the federal government under the Federal Tort Claims Act, missing the deadline to file a lawsuit by over two years.

item.title: Senate pushes ahead with plan to fund government through midterms
item.description: The Senate is moving ahead with a plan to keep the government funded and avoid another shutdown before the midterm elections.

item.title: 8/3: CBS Evening News
item.description: Spokane wildfires force thousands to evacuate; Michigan reports two cyclosporiasis deaths.

item.title: Trump says oil companies should cut gas prices after making "too much money"
item.description: President Trump said U.S. oil companies made "too much money" from high oil prices. "I'm not happy about it," he added.

item.title: 8/3: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Trump says he's giving Iran a "last chance" at diplomacy; Blanche one step closer to confirmation as attorney general.

item.title: Michigan health officials report 2 deaths among cyclosporiasis cases
item.description: Two Michigan residents who had "significant underlying health conditions" have died after contracting cyclosporiasis, the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services said.

item.title: Sheriff in Nancy Guthrie case contradicted himself on ransom note
item.description: Investigators in the disappearance of Nancy Guthrie released two ransom notes, including one contradicting what the Arizona sheriff overseeing the case told CBS News.

item.title: Federal workers sour on government work, decrying eroding job security
item.description: Nearly two-thirds of current and retired U.S. government workers said they wouldn't re-enter public service, according to a recent survey.

item.title: 8/2: Sunday Morning
item.description: Jane Pauley hosts our annual "Money Issue." Featured: Obstacles to home ownership; fighting health insurance denials; Chinese EVs; opposition to AI data centers; American Girl dolls; skin care mogul Scarlett Johansson; roller coasters; the popularity of Bingo!; and is your phone eavesdropping on you?

item.title: The Uplift: The American Dream
item.description: We celebrate the United States ahead of its 250th anniversary with stories about American heroes and pastimes. The founder of e.l.f. Cosmetics shares how he made a massive life change to become a Catholic priest.
